items.a_text: When outcome base rates differ across protected groups and data separation is imperfect, conditional use accuracy equality and error rate equality (false positive and false negative rates) cannot be simultaneously satisfied.
items.b_text: No risk assignment method can simultaneously satisfy calibration within groups, balance for the negative class, and balance for the positive class except in instances allowing perfect prediction or having equal base rates across groups.
items.explanation: Both claims state the same impossibility theorem in algorithmic fairness: calibration and error rate balance cannot be simultaneously achieved when base rates differ across groups and predictions are imperfect.

items.a_text: When recidivism prevalence differs between two groups, a test-fair risk score cannot achieve equal false positive and false negative rates across those groups simultaneously.
items.b_text: When outcome base rates differ across protected groups and data separation is imperfect, conditional use accuracy equality and error rate equality (false positive and false negative rates) cannot be simultaneously satisfied.
items.explanation: Both claims assert the same fundamental impossibility result in algorithmic fairness: when base rates differ across groups, predictive parity (test-fairness/conditional use accuracy equality) and equal error rates cannot be simultaneously satisfied.

items.a_text: Excluding or discounting protected group attributes from a fitting procedure reduces overall prediction accuracy when those attributes share non-redundant associations with the outcome.
